Subject: Quick recap + questions after today's call

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can size a Dedicated path for Meridian: 

- Current priority: move from prototype (hosted API) to a stable, cost-predictable inference tier for customer-facing chat and batch embedding jobs.
- Traffic patterns you described: steady chat load during business hours (09:00–18:00 PT) with peaks around product launches; separate nightly batch embedding jobs (bulk IDs -> 1536-dim vectors).
- Rough per-request token mix you mentioned: median ~220 tokens, 95th ~1200 tokens (long-form summarization).
- Target p95 latency for chat: 350–450ms; acceptable for batch embeddings: several minutes per job.

As next steps, can you confirm the following so we can finalize a Dedicated sizing worksheet: 
1) Peak sustained TPS target for chat (not just concurrency). You mentioned ~6 TPS during peaks — is 6–8 TPS accurate?
2) Expected concurrency per user session (KV cache reuse). Any idea of the average turn count per session?
3) Do you have procurement constraints that would force a Private (VPC/on-prem) decision vs Dedicated?

I've attached a lightweight worksheet and the call recording. Karthik and I will sketch two options: (A) Dedicated pool with H100-80GB-style profile for lower latency per token and (B) mixed pool (A100 / L4) that favors cost for batch-heavy windows.

Proposed short cadence: we will send the sizing worksheet back tomorrow morning and schedule a 30-min sizing review — does 10:00 PT on Tuesday (May 25) work?

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak TPS: our product team expects external chat traffic to reach ~7 TPS sustained for up to 90 minutes during launches, with short spikes to ~12 TPS for a few minutes. So 6–8 TPS capture normal peaks; planning for spikes to 12 is important.
- Concurrency / session: average session is ~3 turns (user -> assistant -> user) but long sessions can go to 8–10 turns during troubleshooting. KV reuse should help.
- Token profile: your numbers are correct — median 200–250, typical heavy prompt+response up to 1400 tokens occasionally.
- Procurement: we prefer Redwood Dedicated for now; Private/VPC is on the roadmap but would require additional approvals (security/compliance doc review). For now assume Dedicated is acceptable.

We're keen to see cost tradeoffs between an H100-focused pool vs mixed configuration and how autoscaling/bursting would handle the ~12 TPS spikes. 10:00 PT Tue works for a quick review.

Alex
Director of Product — Meridian Labs
alex.gopal@meridian.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick recap + questions after today's call

Thanks — adding a technical sizing pass and assumptions so the worksheet we return is actionable. High-level notes: 

Assumptions pulled from Alex's reply: peak sustained chat TPS = 7, short spikes = 12, median tokens/request = 225, 95th = 1,400, session turns typical 3, long 8–10.

Sizing considerations (tradeoffs):
- GPU choices:
  * H100 (80GB / 96GB): best latency per token for long sequences and heavy KV cache; fewer GPUs required for same p95 latency but higher hourly cost.
  * A100 (40GB/80GB): good middle ground for mixed workloads; cheaper than H100 in many clouds; performs well for medium seq lengths.
  * L4 / T4x (40GB-like inference GPUs): very cost-effective for short-median sequences and heavy batching (embeddings), but less efficient for long-form 1400-token responses at low-latency SLOs.

- Concurrency & batching: to hit p95 ~400ms at 7 TPS for a 225-token median, continuous batching with small max-batch (4–8) helps. For 12 TPS spikes, autoscaling + burst pool (additional pre-warmed instances) recommended to avoid queueing.

- KV cache: session-level KV reuse will reduce work for turns beyond the first — plan for cache hit-rate 65–75% in steady state, which reduces effective token work per request.

Preliminary recommendation (deliverable for Tue):
- Option 1 (Performance-first): Dedicated H100 pool sized to sustain 8 TPS with headroom for spikes to 12 via burst capacity (target p95 chat latency 350ms).
- Option 2 (Cost-balanced): Mixed pool (2x A100 nodes + 1x L4 cluster for batch embeddings) with routing policies: chat -> A100 primary, L4 for embeddings / opportunistic burst when queue low. This lowers monthly spend ~25–40% depending on cloud pricing.

I'll attach the worksheet with run-rate estimates, a simple concurrency model, and a suggested autoscaling policy (min/max nodes, warm buffer). Jordan — will you share any specific cloud region preferences and whether you want a single-region Dedicated pool or multi-region? That affects both latency for users and pricing (eg, H100 availability).

-Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
